whatItIs.text: White sugar with molasses left in (or added back) — the moisture and acid of the molasses are what make bakes chewy and butterscotchy.

historyNote.text: Sugar was first produced from sugarcane in the Indian subcontinent — Sanskrit śarkarā is the root of 'sugar' — and reached Europe via Arabic Sicily and Spain; beet sugar, first industrialised in Prussia in 1801, is the starting point of the modern industry.

howToChoose.text: Choose by feel: soft and clumpy is fresh, hard as brick just needs re-moistening (a slice of bread in the jar overnight); light vs dark is simply molasses level.

storage.text: Keep airtight at room temperature so it stays soft. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: dry-goods storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Hardened brown sugar dissolves back in warm recipes, grates fine, or can be blitzed; it also rubs beautifully onto pork and salmon.
